summary.headline: Syngene Q1 FY27 revenue fell 16% YoY to INR 736 crore and EBITDA margin was 12%; FY27 guided to single-digit rupee revenue decline.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 736 crore, down 16% YoY, driven by absence of Zoetis offtake and attrition of some research services clients. Operating EBITDA was INR 91 crore (12% margin), hit by a INR 50 crore forex hedge loss, partly offset by cost optimisation. Profit after tax before exceptionals was INR 1 crore; reported PAT was negative INR 9 crore after a INR 10 crore net exceptional charge for termination benefits. Management revised FY27 guidance to a single-digit rupee revenue decline (call summary also cites mid-single-digit and low-single-digit decline) with mid-20s EBITDA margin, framing FY27 as a transition year with growth returning from FY28.

financial_highlights.change: includes INR 50 crore forex hedge loss

financial_highlights.metric: Profit after tax before exceptional items

financial_highlights.change: mainly Bayview facility, plus automation and AI
versus about INR 1,800 crore last year per analyst

segments.name: Research services (discovery and clinical)
segments.commentary: Accounted for 78% of Q1 revenue; management cited attrition of some clients who were lost on cost, as the company deliberately stepped back from commoditised services. Clinical research is a small base but expected to grow strongly from this fiscal.

segments.name: CDMO (small and large molecule)
segments.commentary: Accounted for 22% of Q1 revenue. Zoetis offtake was absent this quarter; Mangalore small-molecule utilisation expected to ramp this year, and Bayview biologics facility targeted to be operational later this year with revenue from FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided to a single-digit decline in rupee terms; analyst question cited a low-single-digit decline and a mid-single-digit decline was also referenced in the Q&A.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided in the mid-20s, relying on a stronger H2 with H1 the weakest period; Q4 is seasonally the strongest quarter.
Management expects a return to profitable and sustainable growth from FY28, with double-digit growth targeted from next fiscal.
Zoetis is not expected to fall to zero in FY28; it has inventory for a couple of years and delivery obligations in H2 FY27. Zoetis FY28 forecast expected by year-end.
Bayview will not be capitalised in FY27; minimal Bayview expenses expected in the P&L this year.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex about INR 70 crore, mainly Bayview facility plus automation and AI platforms; further investment planned through the year to operationalise Bayview.

Bayview (US biologics) to be operationalised later this year; customers will be locked in only after operationalisation. One or two expressions of interest converted into project-based CMO requirements in the US, with revenue from next year.
Mangalore site was under-utilised; lock-ins for commercial and clinical molecules secured and significant utilisation ramp-up expected this fiscal and further in FY28.

Stelis facility: customers signed and batches taken; ramp-up during this year and into next year. Molecules mostly clinical or development stage, with no large-volume commercial molecule from Unit 3 yet.
demand_pricing: Management said the company drifted into commoditised research services with pricing pressure; it is deliberately not competing on low-cost offerings, leading to client attrition.
Biologics dependence on one large customer (Zoetis) cost about $50 million of revenue impact; spare capacity created and being filled with new customers.

Pipeline for large-molecule CDMO is described as robust; US-based capacity seen as benefiting from tariffs and Make in US demand, and Biosecure Act seen as helping shift molecules from China to India.
New commercial organisation led by Abhijit Zutshi (ex-CCO, Biocon Generics) is building segmentation and business development; management expects RFP-to-revenue gestation.
Management said green shoots are visible and will give more clarity from next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 revenue guidance cut from roughly flat to a decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to the loss of Zoetis contribution this quarter; gap expected to be filled by other customers only by fiscal year-end, so guidance is a slight decline.

qa_highlights.question: Will the revenue gap be filled by clinical or commercial molecules?
qa_highlights.answer: A combination; Mangalore has commercial and clinical lock-ins with significant utilisation ramp this year and into FY28, while Bayview revenue depends on discussions to be converted by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Why did discovery clients attrite, and what is the value-added vs commoditised split?
qa_highlights.answer: Attrition was driven by cost-based competition in commoditised services that management chose not to match; the split was deferred to an offline discussion.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the revenue decline is due to Zoetis, and is Zoetis now at zero?
qa_highlights.answer: Zoetis impact was about $50 million; not zero, as Zoetis holds inventory for a couple of years with H2 FY27 delivery obligations and is not expected to be zero in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What gives visibility to a strong H2 margin pick-up to hit mid-20s EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Deepak Jain cited H2 revenue uptick, savings from FY26 cost actions and continued cost initiatives, seasonally strong Q4, and steady-state margins historically above mid-20s.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cost measures and the margin outlook for FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost optimisation covers people and operating expenses, with technology as a lever; Bayview not capitalised this year. Management said it is too early to comment on FY28 margins but does not expect flat margins.

risks_watch: H1 FY27 revenue and margin weakness; guidance depends on H2 ramp across Mangalore, Stelis and Bayview.
Zoetis run-off: delivery obligations in H2 FY27 and FY28 forecast due by year-end.
Client attrition in research services and pricing pressure in commoditised discovery work.
Bayview operationalisation timing and conversion of expressions of interest into contracts.
Forex hedge losses (INR 50 crore in Q1) and their effect on reported margins; cash decline from INR 1,800 crore last year to INR 1,541 crore.
summary.management_tone: Candid and cautious: management openly acknowledged a transition year, loss of a major customer and over-reliance on commoditised work, while staying confident on CDMO and AI-led discovery recovery from FY28. Specifics on pipeline, long-term growth and discovery segment splits were deferred to next quarter or offline.
key_quotes: FY27 is a year of transition for Syngene. It is a year of course correction, strategic renewal, and disciplined execution under a new leadership team.
The loss of that business has had a significant impact on our near-term financial performance and has reinforced the importance of building a more diversified and resilient commercial portfolio.
Otherwise, it becomes a race to the bottom because it becomes commoditized and then you're just basically providing very low-margin services, which is what has happened to us.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided to a single-digit rupee decline (the brief also cites low- and mid-single-digit variants, so midpoint -5% is a best estimate) with mid-20s EBITDA margin; growth returns with double-digit targeted from FY28, backed by Bayview (live FY28), Mangalore and Stelis ramp-ups and spare capacity being filled, but customer lock-ins are only partly quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Mid-20s EBITDA margin guided for FY27 versus 12% in Q1 (including INR 50 crore forex hedge loss), relying on H2 revenue uptick, FY26 cost-action savings and seasonally strong Q4.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Bayview US biologics facility to be operationalised later this year (INR 70 crore Q1 capex, not capitalised in FY27), and Mangalore and Stelis ramp-ups are under way with lock-ins secured; revenue from FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided to a single-digit rupee decline (midpoint about -5%), with double-digit growth targeted from FY28 once Mangalore, Stelis and Bayview ramps and spare capacity fill, but customer lock-ins are only partly quantified.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Q1 capex about INR 70 crore with further investment planned through the year to operationalise Bayview; no new capacity size or utilisation level disclosed, and Mangalore was described as under-utilised, which argues against a fresh build near term.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance was just cut to a single-digit decline, with Q1 revenue down 16% YoY and H1 flagged as the weakest period.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 FY27 weakness and dependence on an H2 ramp across Mangalore, Stelis and Bayview leave the mid-20s margin and single-digit decline guidance exposed; the brief also cites low- and mid-single-digit variants, so the exact revenue cut is unclear.

rows.label: Return to double-digit growth from FY28
rows.why: Management targets double-digit sustainable growth from next fiscal, but Q1 revenue fell 16% YoY and the Zoetis FY28 forecast is due only at year-end.

rows.label: Zoetis run-off and FY28 forecast
rows.why: Zoetis impact about $50 million; inventory covers a couple of years and delivery obligations fall in H2 FY27, with the FY28 forecast due by year-end, so it is not expected to reach zero.

rows.label: US biologics CMO wins from Biosecure and tariffs
rows.why: One or two expressions of interest converted into project-based US CMO requirements with revenue from next year; the pipeline is described as robust, but conversion to contracts is still pending.

tone.note: Management was confident on the CDMO pipeline, Mangalore and Stelis ramps and FY28 recovery, but cautious on H1 weakness and client attrition from commoditised research work; analysts pushed on the guidance cut, the Zoetis run-off and the H2 margin path to mid-20s.

oneOffs.what: INR 50 crore forex hedge loss in Q1 FY27 depressed operating EBITDA (margin 12%)
INR 10 crore net exceptional charge for employee termination benefits (reported PAT negative INR 9 crore)

quality.why: Revenue fell 16% YoY to INR 736 crore, so there is no growth to explain; the decline is driven by the loss of Zoetis offtake and client attrition in research services, which are recurring headwinds rather than one-offs. The INR 50 crore forex hedge loss is the major one-off that depressed Q1 profit (EBITDA margin 12%), and the INR 10 crore exceptional termination charge depressed reported PAT furt
